atomic_claim_or_observation: In a September 25 memorandum to Johnson, Vice President Humphrey recorded Malik as saying that Suharto had specifically asked him to convey gratitude for U.S. encouragement of Indonesian anti-Communist forces dating back to 1963.
claim_type: Contemporaneous secondhand report of a political statement
confidence: Medium: the memo directly records Malik's statement, but Malik is reporting Suharto's message and the 1963 U.S. activity needs separate archival corroboration
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d222, paragraph 2.
next_verification: Locate the original 1963-1965 U.S. diplomatic, intelligence and covert-action records and an Indonesian-side record of the message.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humphrey recorded Malik's statements that Indonesia sought rice from the U.S., Burma, Thailand and Taiwan; was entering an agreement for Taiwan to process cotton into clothing; needed food and cotton for troops; and intended to use the army for public-works engineering after confrontation ended. The memo also records disagreement between Malik and Suharto adviser Soejono over whether early U.S. reluctance was politically prudent.
confidence: Medium for Malik's attributed statements and the reported disagreement; the Taiwan agreement, rice purchases, troop distribution and public-works plan need independent records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d222, paragraphs 11-28 and source note.
next_verification: Obtain the Taiwan agreement, rice contracts and shipping/receipt records, Indonesian Army plans and both September 25 participants' notes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the September 27 Rusk-Malik conversation, Rusk said he had raised Soviet cooperation with Gromyko, who gave no indication of the Soviet position; Rusk emphasized non-discriminatory treatment of creditors and said a settlement implying Soviet repayment at Western creditors' expense would create U.S. political problems. Malik predicted the USSR would accept the Tokyo principles, but this is not evidence of Soviet agreement.
confidence: High for the recorded exchange; Soviet acceptance and actual payment priority remain unverified; this is Part I of III only
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d223, paragraphs 30-34.
next_verification: Read parts II and III, original Tokyo Agreed Minute, Soviet bilateral debt agreement and creditor payment records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: At his September 27 meeting with Johnson, Malik said the PKI had suffered a major setback but could recover if the government failed to improve economic conditions; he described food, clothing, industrial reactivation, infrastructure and inflation as urgent issues. Johnson urged coordination of external resources with a concrete recovery plan developed with an objective institution such as the IMF.
claim_type: Contemporaneous secret White House conversation memorandum
confidence: High for the recorded exchange; Malik's forecast and the aid-policy relationship do not by themselves establish actual outcomes or a causal effect
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d224, paragraphs 30-39.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian stabilization budget, IMF/IBRD program documents, aid commitments/disbursements and prices/output data for 1966-1968.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In an October 27 cable, Ambassador Green assessed that Indonesia's emerging political order would be planned, built and sponsored by the Army, which he expected to remain a dominant political force; he described army-led government, regional administrative posts and national enterprises as part of this development.
confidence: High for Green's assessment; the distribution of actual authority requires Indonesian administrative, business and military records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d225, paragraphs 1-2.
next_verification: Compare provincial appointment lists, state-enterprise boards, pepelrada records, Army plans and Indonesian political statements.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green advocated U.S. support for Suharto's civic-action program as a way to give the Army a constructive role, curb corruption and unwanted political activity, generate visible public-welfare gains, and strengthen U.S. influence with the leaders expected to run Indonesia; he proposed spares, sales, noncombat items and officer training.
confidence: High for stated intent and proposals; not proof Congress, the President or the recipient approved each measure
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d225, paragraphs 3-6.
next_verification: Trace d226, later authorization, program accounts, equipment lists, training rosters and Indonesian project reports.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On November 1 the Joint Chiefs said there was no direct military requirement for an Indonesian MAP but recommended a $6 million FY1967 materials-and-services program and a $6 million FY1968 planning guideline; they warned an FY1968-only program would arrive mainly in 1968-1969 and suggested possible Mundt Amendment treatment, contingent on available funds and supplemental appropriations.
confidence: High for the recommendation; the memo does not itself establish final appropriation, legal inclusion or delivery
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d226, paragraphs 1-4.
next_verification: Find final Defense/AID approval, FY1967 supplemental appropriation, Mundt Amendment country listing and shipment/inventory records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On December 7 the State Department called the Army's civic-action program a blueprint with broadly stated needs, argued Indonesia could begin basic labor-intensive works with existing tools, and advised that any U.S. program initially support projects already underway rather than U.S.-planned studies; officials worried planning involvement could shift resource and success/failure responsibility to Washington.
confidence: High for the Department's stated analysis and conditions; actual field projects and subsequent U.S. implementation need separate proof
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d227, paragraphs 1-7.
next_verification: Read the referenced December 1 cable, project list, Army reports and 1967 AID/MAP monitoring.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A February 1967 interagency National Intelligence Estimate concluded that Indonesia's need for foreign economic assistance, expected mainly from the U.S., Japan and Western Europe, would virtually ensure continuation of Western-leaning foreign policies; it also forecast that Sukarno would lose effective power and noted likely civilian-military conflict. These were U.S. intelligence judgments and forecasts.
confidence: High that the estimate made these judgments; low as proof of eventual outcomes or causal effect of aid
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d228, conclusions A-C and source note.
next_verification: Compare subsequent foreign-policy decisions, aid commitments, Indonesian records and other intelligence assessments; retain forecast/outcome distinction.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a February 17 briefing, Ambassador Green presented Humphrey with a strongly anti-PKI account of the 1965 coup and killings, including a 300,000-400,000 death estimate and a claim that a trained women's corps killed the generals; he also said U.S. firmness in Vietnam had benefited the Indonesian Army. This is evidence of Green's official narrative, not independent confirmation of those disputed claims.
claim_type: Contemporaneous U.S. official narrative and policy briefing
confidence: High for the recorded briefing; low or disputed for uncorroborated causal, coup and women's-corps assertions
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d229, paragraphs 12-29.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian military/PKI records, survivor testimony, forensic and regional research; identify records Green relied on and any omitted dissenting assessments.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow sought authority for a U.S. contribution of up to one-third of Indonesia's estimated $210-240 million 1967 aid need, capped at $85 million; his memo said $36 million was already committed and the remainder could include $30-40 million PL-480 and $10-20 million support assistance, with AID procurement limited to U.S. sources. A FRUS note records Johnson later accepting the one-third offer on the assumption Japan and Europe supplied the other two-thirds.
claim_type: Contemporaneous White House aid proposal and editorially cited approval note
confidence: High for the proposed ceiling and conditional approach; medium for amounts committed absent financial ledgers; not equivalent to an $85 million disbursement
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d230, paragraphs 11-25 and footnote 4.
next_verification: Retrieve the February 16 Agriculture-AID request, Johnson's February 23 note, IGG commitments, AID vouchers, CCC accounts and Indonesian receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow's February 21 memorandum recorded Green's view that U.S. Vietnam policy had favorably affected Indonesian military developments, that this effect should not be discussed publicly, and that aid should be sufficiently timely and politically useful to consolidate the new government's position and encourage Japan/Europe to contribute.
claim_type: Contemporaneous White House summary of ambassador's views
confidence: High for reported U.S. policy thinking; Green's causal claims and intended effects are not independently established
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d231, paragraphs 11-49.
next_verification: Compare private and public U.S. policy statements, Japanese/European donor records and Indonesian views.

atomic_claim_or_observation: McNamara's March 1 memorandum put total U.S. MAP to Indonesia at $63.2 million for 1950-1965, about $59 million in 1959-1965, including $40 million for the Army with more than 100,000 small arms and about 2,000 vehicles; he said $3 million in engineering equipment had supported Army civic-action programs during 1962-1964.
confidence: High that the Secretary cited these figures; precise delivered quantities and valuation require Defense and Indonesian inventory records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d232, paragraphs 15-18.
next_verification: Reconcile MAP grants, procurement and delivery records with Indonesian military inventories; identify vehicle versus truck categories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: McNamara said the U.S. spent roughly $5 million to train about 2,100 Indonesian military personnel in the United States, continued training during 1963-1965 after suspending equipment shipments, and retained military attaches and a skeletal Defense Liaison Group after MAP ended; he described the civic-action officer program as preparing Army personnel for government management.
claim_type: Contemporaneous Defense Department retrospective of military contact and training
confidence: High for the Secretary's account; named rosters, budgets and Indonesian evaluations remain to be checked
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d232, paragraphs 14-20.
next_verification: Obtain student rosters, school curricula, DLG staffing and communications, canceled-program files, and Indonesian service records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: McNamara argued that prior U.S. military training, equipment and continued sympathy encouraged Indonesian Army leaders to believe they could count on U.S. support when they turned against the PKI and later Sukarno; he expressly cautioned that U.S. programs were not solely responsible or necessarily the major cause.
claim_type: Contemporaneous U.S. Secretary of Defense causal assessment
confidence: High for the Secretary's stated belief; causal weight is an official retrospective claim, not independently demonstrated
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d232, paragraphs 12-24.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian officer correspondence, alumni networks, unit actions and alternate explanations; separate training influence from covert operational direction.

atomic_claim_or_observation: McNamara reported that officer training resumed in September 1966 at an FY1967 cost of $400,000, that the U.S. had decided during the previous week to add $2 million to FY1967 MAP for civic-action spares and equipment, and planned a $6 million FY1968 MAP; the memo does not prove all funds were spent or items delivered.
confidence: High for the reported decision/plan; delivery and use remain open
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d232, paragraphs 21-22.
next_verification: Compare appropriations, training rosters, MAP project authorizations, requisitions, invoices and Indonesian receiving records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A March 15 U.S. Embassy cable reported that the MPRS had withdrawn Sukarno's mandate and Suharto had been sworn in as Acting President on March 12; Green then interpreted the session as a negotiated gain for civilian groups and military factions. The first statement is supported in the cable's note by a separate cited telegram, while the political reading is Green's assessment.
claim_type: Contemporaneous diplomatic report with cited telegram and ambassadorial analysis
confidence: High for what the Embassy reported; use MPRS decree and Indonesian records for the formal act and do not treat Green's interpretation as neutral
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d233, paragraphs 1-2 and footnote 2.
next_verification: Retrieve the March 12 MPRS decree, session transcript, Acting President oath record and Indonesian press.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green's March 15 cable forecast shifting party-military alliances, pressure for cabinet posts, possible postponement of elections beyond July 1968, Suharto's continued reliance on the armed forces and possible further operations against isolated left groups; these were forecasts, not established outcomes.
confidence: High for the cable's forecasts; low as evidence that each predicted event occurred
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d233, paragraphs 2-8.
next_verification: Compare later MPRS/election laws, cabinet appointments, regional military orders and contemporaneous Indonesian party records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In an April 25 internal letter, Green agreed with a U.S. political analysis that the military was unlikely to withdraw from an active role and might seek more power; he discussed guaranteed representation for the military and Action Fronts alongside efforts to enlist political parties, while advising that elections should wait until economic rehabilitation was underway.
claim_type: Contemporaneous secret U.S. diplomatic political analysis
confidence: High for Green's view; the referenced Berger letter is missing and proposals are not evidence of Indonesian adoption
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d234, paragraphs a-e and f.
next_verification: Find Berger's March 31 letter and compare with MPRS election laws, parliamentary seat allocation and party records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green suggested that appointing Malik as First Minister under Suharto could help preserve their relationship and make Malik Suharto's deputy across political and economic affairs; he also judged Malik politically dependent on Suharto. This was an ambassadorial recommendation/assessment, not an enacted appointment.
confidence: High for the recommendation and Green's assessment; no evidence here of a formal appointment or Indonesian acceptance
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d234, paragraphs h-i.
next_verification: Compare cabinet appointment instruments, Indonesian correspondence and Malik's own records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On June 27 U.S. talking points said the Scheveningen donor meeting had agreed to cover a projected $200 million Indonesian balance-of-payments gap; the U.S. Department separately claimed it had postponed $51 million of debt payments falling due July 1966-December 1967, provided $77 million in new aid and committed another $32 million, for about $160 million through December 1967.
confidence: High that the Department presented these figures; medium for comparable totals because postponement, commitment and aid-provision categories differ
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d235, paragraphs 2-3 and footnote 3.
next_verification: Reconcile creditor schedules and U.S. AID/PL-480/CCC disbursements with IGG minutes and Indonesian treasury receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The June 27 talking points treated Indonesian economic advisers' IMF-supported stabilization program as a basis for international confidence and continued aid; they also stressed the investment law, handling U.S. businesses through authorized officials and continued policy performance as conditions for sustaining private investment and assistance.
claim_type: Contemporaneous U.S. assistance and investment policy guidance
confidence: High for the Department's stated policy linkage; the full donor chair report and individual investment agreements were not reviewed
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d235, paragraphs 14-26 and footnotes 5-6.
next_verification: Read Scheveningen chair report, IMF program reviews, MPRS investment law implementation and company-level investment contracts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green reported that Suharto questioned whether Washington prioritized Indonesia and complained that expected dollar loans might not materialize, that the U.S. might push unwanted PL-480 sales, and that the FY1968 package could be mostly commodities; Suharto reportedly said the Ampera cabinet program assumed continuing U.S. aid and that uncertainty could force major budget changes.
claim_type: Ambassador's account of a private meeting with Suharto
confidence: High for Green's report of Suharto's statements; the underlying U.S. loan decisions and Indonesian budget assumptions require original records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d236, paragraphs 1-4.
next_verification: Obtain Suharto's and Green's notes, Widjojo's Washington brief, FY1967/68 AID loan decisions and Ampera budget planning papers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green told Suharto that Washington supported his government and wanted regular direct communication; the cable also records Suharto's preference for rice and dollar import loans, acceptance of PL-480 cotton but opposition to finished textiles, a stated need for 150,000 bales of raw cotton by April 1968, and a reported request for as much PL-480 rice as possible in 1967.
confidence: High for the recorded exchange; cotton quantity, rice procurement and terms need contracts and Indonesian planning documents
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d236, paragraphs 4-7.
next_verification: Retrieve grain and cotton agreements, loan terms, shipment records, textile-industry capacity data and Indonesian cabinet minutes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green reported that he was authorized to promise 2,000 uniform sets and 32,000 jungle boots for military civic-action personnel and described officer support for expanding the civic mission; Suharto requested more import loans, PL-480 rice, and expanded food-for-work, which he said needed rupiah financing for local costs. Authorization and reported discussion do not prove delivery or final distribution.
claim_type: Contemporaneous U.S. aid authorization as reported in embassy cable
confidence: High for the reported authorization and requests; no receiving receipts or unit-level distribution records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d236, paragraphs 8-9.
next_verification: Find procurement, freight, delivery, customs, military issue and local-currency food-for-work accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humphrey's July 14 memo cited Suharto's doubt about U.S. aid priority and argued for high-priority, multilateral assistance involving Japan and Europe; reporting Green's account, it also says Suharto expressed continued support for U.S. Vietnam policy and hinted that bombing North Vietnamese dikes could cause floods.
claim_type: Contemporaneous Vice Presidential policy memorandum based partly on Green's report
confidence: High for what Humphrey wrote; the dike statement is secondhand and does not establish a formal Indonesian government position or operational proposal
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d237, paragraphs 11-18 and footnote 4.
next_verification: Compare d236's underlying cable and separate Vietnamese/Indonesian diplomatic records; do not infer an order or planned attack.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In July, two Indonesian Army officers told Rostow they sought a personal communication channel between Suharto and Johnson and believed U.S. aid follow-through disappointed; Rostow warned that it was unclear whether they spoke for Suharto and they might be advancing their own influence, yet recommended reassessing aid and a possible presidential relationship.
claim_type: Contemporaneous White House account of intermediary diplomacy
confidence: High for Rostow's memorandum and his stated uncertainty; the attached meeting record and officers' own messages are absent
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d238, paragraphs 6-10 and footnotes 3-4.
next_verification: Retrieve the July 19 attached memorandum, Humphrey meeting record, Embassy telegrams 10175/10759 and Indonesian travel/meeting files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow wrote on July 22 that the U.S. needed at least 100,000 tons of rice to meet its 1967 commitments and would otherwise leave nearly $10 million unsatisfied; he considered using FY1968 resources as a cash loan but warned this would worsen next year's shortfall and risk Indonesian disappointment.
claim_type: Contemporaneous secret White House aid-accounting memorandum
confidence: High for the internal U.S. assessment; it identifies a prospective commitment gap, not proof of a final contract, shipment or non-delivery
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d239, paragraphs 51-59.
next_verification: Compare PL-480 purchase authorizations, rice contracts, U.S. commitment ledgers, arrival records and Indonesian allocation data.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Notes of Johnson's July 25 meeting record Rusk saying $200 million was planned within the Indonesia donor consortium and that Congress might be asked to select countries for foreign-aid reductions; the editor notes no record was found for the next day's Indonesia meeting.
claim_type: Top-secret presidential meeting notes and archival access-gap note
confidence: High for the recorded statement and missing-record note; the $200 million planning figure is not an audited amount disbursed
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d240, paragraphs 47-54 and source note.
next_verification: Locate the July 26 meeting record, consortium pledge schedules and congressional foreign-assistance reduction files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A U.S. paper prepared for the NSC described the New Order as established and Sukarno as politically eliminated, and treated Indonesia as a strategic test of the U.S.-backed modernization model.
confidence: High for the paper's stated view; not a neutral measure of Indonesian political control or public opinion
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d241, paragraphs 1-4.
next_verification: Compare MPRS decrees, Indonesian cabinet and military records, party activity and contemporaneous Indonesian press.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same U.S. paper reported the 1967 donor package and a roughly $197 million pledge/furnishing table, including a $65 million U.S. share; it also described a $200 million aid target and debt rescheduling as separate categories.
claim_type: U.S. aid and debt accounting in policy paper
confidence: High for what the paper reports; pledge, furnishing, debt relief and physical delivery are different accounting stages
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d241, aid and debt sections.
next_verification: Reconcile IGG minutes and donor schedules with AID, Treasury, World Bank and Indonesian receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Gaud and Freeman reported $30 million in AID loans and an $8 million PL-480 cotton credit as actions already taken, while proposing additional rice, tobacco and cotton measures to close a stated $27 million gap in the U.S. 1967 contribution.
claim_type: Interagency proposal and reported prior actions
confidence: High for the memorandum's accounting and recommendations; loan agreement, obligation, disbursement and export may differ
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d242, paragraphs 1-7.
next_verification: Find loan authorizations, PL-480 contracts, AID obligations, shipment records and final U.S. contribution ledger.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The August 8 proposal included 100,000 tons of PL-480 rice but made further assistance conditional on satisfactory Indonesian agricultural self-help; the memo said rice availability competed with Vietnam, Africa and commercial sales.
confidence: High for the stated proposal and supply concern; no final approval or rice delivery shown
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d242.
next_verification: Compare presidential decisions, PL-480 allocations, Indonesian crop and procurement data, and arrival records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow's August 8 briefing identified 100,000 tons of rice as central to the 1967 aid discussion and asked the NSC to plan a donor-supported program for 1968 and later years.
confidence: High for agenda; it was not itself a decision to buy or deliver rice
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d243.
next_verification: Read NSC minutes and subsequent Presidential Determinations and commodity files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The August 9 NSC discussion considered a possible $60 million 1968 package consisting of $20 million each in AID, rice and cotton, with a possible $40 million gap against a $100 million U.S. share.
confidence: High for the discussion; figures were planning estimates, not a final appropriation or pledge
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d244.
next_verification: Compare the final FY1968 appropriation, AID obligation ledger, PL-480 and cotton contracts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the same NSC record, USIA Director Marks described a low-key information operation and Johnson called Indonesia a possible showcase; the notes do not define the operation as covert or show that showcase proposals were implemented.
confidence: High for the recorded remarks; the scope and methods of the USIA activity remain unspecified
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d244 and footnotes.
next_verification: Obtain USIA country-program plans and appropriations, and distinguish overt information work from any separately documented covert program.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A September U.S. planning memo reported Indonesian expectations ranging from roughly $325 million to $350 million in total 1968 foreign aid and U.S. requests of about $100-$150 million; U.S. staff assessed a package nearer $80 million.
claim_type: Reported requests and U.S. planning estimates
confidence: High for the reported conversation and calculations; attributed expectations were not approved commitments
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d245.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian budget and donor submissions with the final Amsterdam/IGG pledge tables.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green's October Cabinet presentation linked the Indonesian political transition to U.S. security interests, foreign aid and private investment; it presented Indonesian alignment and the Vietnam issue through a U.S. policy frame.
confidence: High for Green's argument; it does not establish Indonesian motives or a causal effect of U.S. Vietnam policy
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d246.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian cabinet records and independent diplomatic accounts; locate the referenced briefing and Johnson-Green conversation.

atomic_claim_or_observation: At a November 4 meeting Suharto reportedly sought about $150 million in U.S. aid, rice and cotton for 1968, while Humphrey reiterated a one-third donor formula, warned Congress had not approved the aid, and asked that requests go through Ambassador Green rather than out-of-channel contacts.
claim_type: Ambassador's report of private aid diplomacy
confidence: High for the contents of Humphrey's report; a private meeting record is not a verbatim transcript, and no firm U.S. pledge was made
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d247, paragraphs 1-12.
next_verification: Find Indonesian notes, Green's reporting, congressional appropriations, donor agreements and shipment/receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humphrey later reported that Suharto and Malaysia's prime minister tied Southeast Asian security to the U.S. position in Vietnam, but the editorial note explicitly records that no aid promise was made at the November visit.
claim_type: Editorial summary of reported political statements
confidence: High for the editorial note; political statements remain attributed and are not aid policy decisions
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d248.
next_verification: Locate Humphrey's original report, meeting notes and U.S. appropriations record.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow recommended a 1968 U.S. aid package of up to $110 million, described as one-third of the nine-nation donor package; Johnson marked approval of the package on November 21.
confidence: High for the documented approval; appropriations, external donor performance and actual disbursement remained conditions
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d249 and presidential annotation.
next_verification: Match approval to congressional appropriations, IGG pledges, AID obligation records and Indonesian receipt ledgers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a December conversation Johnson said at least half of U.S. aid would be PL-480 food; Malik said Indonesia had shifted its ration mix to 40 percent rice and 60 percent bulgur as rice supply fell short of demand.
claim_type: Presidential conversation and attributed ration report
confidence: High for recorded statements; the ration shares and actual household distribution are not independently verified
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d250.
next_verification: Check Indonesian food-ministry/Bulog ration orders, import and warehouse ledgers, and urban/rural distribution surveys.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Embassy's January 1968 retrospective said a serious 1967 rice shortage and doubled inflation left the average Indonesian with no more rice at year-end than at the beginning and at a higher price; it also said the New Order had not built a nonmilitary political base.
confidence: High for the Embassy's assessment; only summary conclusions are published, and no household survey or full underlying report is reproduced
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d251, summary and conclusions only.
next_verification: Obtain the complete A-358 airgram and cross-check rice prices, distribution, wages, inflation and local political organization.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A February 1968 White House memo described Indonesian requests for hundreds of thousands of tons of bulgur and U.S. milling capacity limits, plus proposed expansion whose timing and market were uncertain.
confidence: High for the stated estimates and proposals; not proof of a signed sale or delivery
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d252.
next_verification: Compare USDA milling plans, contracts, export manifests, port records and Indonesian distribution records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Embassy's February 1968 policy airgram said the United States had a heavy stake in New Order success, had quietly influenced senior leaders, and should avoid involvement so overt that it replaced Indonesian initiative or appeared as Americanization.
confidence: High for explicit U.S. policy language; self-reported influence does not establish the reach or effectiveness of each channel
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d253, sections II-III.
next_verification: Find referenced policy cables, meeting notes, adviser instructions and Indonesian records of advice received and acted upon.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same airgram advocated using the IMF, IBRD and donor group as collective pressure on Indonesia, and treated Western-trained Indonesian economic advisers as intermediaries through whom U.S. programs could be adapted and influence exercised.
claim_type: U.S. influence mechanism described in policy paper
confidence: High for the written strategy; effect on Indonesian decisions requires separate evidence
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d253, sections III.B-C and conclusion.
next_verification: Compare IMF/IBRD conditionality and donor minutes with Bappenas, cabinet and budget records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Embassy proposed participant and team training, book distribution and selective limits on U.S. personnel in sensitive fields; it characterized Indonesian social relationships using the U.S.-devised 'third culture' and 'Bapak' framework.
confidence: High for the policy proposal; the cultural framework is an interested U.S. analytic construct, not an independently validated description
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d253, sections III.C-F.
next_verification: Find USIA/AID program records, participant lists and Indonesian assessments; compare Indonesian social-science scholarship.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State said an April 14, 1967 U.S.-Indonesian agreement covered civic-action assistance and that the program had operated for about a year; it defined the U.S. role as supporting public works with direct civilian benefit, not broader Indonesian military commercial or barracks activities.
confidence: High for the U.S. policy letter's description; verify the agreement text and implementation separately
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d254, paragraphs 1-3.
next_verification: Retrieve 18 UST 384, MAP equipment and training records, project lists, and Army G-4/local project ledgers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The March 1968 State letter said U.S. officials wanted counterinsurgency kept in Indonesian hands and, under current circumstances, did not seek MAP support for uprisings in West Borneo or West New Guinea; it left future assistance open.
confidence: High for the policy position; this letter alone cannot establish that no other U.S. channel provided relevant support
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d254, paragraphs 3-9.
next_verification: Search Defense, CIA, Embassy and Indonesian operational files for other assistance, intelligence exchange, logistics and training.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rostow urged vigorous follow-up on a possible PL-480 wheat sale and described food sales as leverage for Indonesian dietary changes; this memorandum does not establish a completed sale.
claim_type: Proposed food sale and policy leverage
confidence: High for the stated strategy; sale, receipt and dietary effect remain unverified
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d255.
next_verification: Find approval, contract, export and Indonesian ration records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a May meeting with Widjojo, U.S. officials linked food assistance and Japanese participation to Indonesian policy choices, including oil supply commitments and investor confidence; the U.S. side voiced concern about aid misuse and domestic political constraints.
confidence: High for the recorded conversation; statements are attributed and no agreement or policy change is proven
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d256.
next_verification: Find Indonesian meeting notes, oil ministry/company contracts, Japanese donor records and AID decisions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: An INR assessment said the June 1968 cabinet reshuffle raised civilian ministers from 14 to 17 and reduced military officers from 9 to 6, interpreting the change as implementation of an MPRS decree and reduction of presidential staff influence.
claim_type: U.S. intelligence assessment of cabinet composition
confidence: High for the assessment's contents; verify counts, portfolios and legal effect in Indonesian official records
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d257.
next_verification: Obtain the cabinet appointment decree, MPRS resolution, ministry roster and contemporary Indonesian press.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The June 18 aid memorandum proposed a $110 million regular U.S. share plus $46 million in wheat/bulgur, including rice, cotton/yarn and an AID development loan; additional fall food and cotton assistance was also contemplated.
confidence: High for the proposal; components occupy different program and budget categories and should not be counted as delivered aid
basis_and_limitations: FRUS XXVI d258.

next_verification: Compare Thai and Japanese records, final observer terms, U.S. UN delegation documents and the underlying Article 19 concern.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Sept. 1 SNIE said the PKI claimed three million members and characterized it as Indonesia’s best-organized and most dynamic political entity.
claim_type: Intelligence assessment citing party membership claim
confidence: High that the estimate says this; membership and comparative judgment are not independently verified.
basis_and_limitations: It labels the total as a PKI claim and the ranking as U.S. analysis.
next_verification: Find PKI membership and dues registers and provincial counts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Sept. 1 SNIE forecast that if Sukarno remained in power the PKI might gain enough state influence in two or three years for Indonesia to be termed a Communist state.
confidence: High for the forecast; not evidence it came true.
basis_and_limitations: The source note says approved Sept. 10; forecast rests on U.S. assumptions and omitted discussion.
next_verification: Compare with Indonesian institutional records and underlying estimate.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The SNIE forecast an initial non-Communist coalition after Sukarno’s early death or incapacity, with the PKI retaining an important share and the military unlikely to risk civil war for immediate rollback.
confidence: High for the forecast; not a confirmed Army decision or actual outcome.
basis_and_limitations: Scenario estimate, not an observed succession plan.
next_verification: Compare underlying estimate with Indonesian succession plans and military records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green reported that Sukarno criticized U.S. media, named Time, Life and Newsweek, and said anti-U.S. feeling and demonstrations would continue while U.S. publications defamed Indonesia and its leaders.
confidence: High that Green recorded this; exact wording moderate because no transcript exists.
basis_and_limitations: The report is not a verbatim record and does not establish public opinion or media effects.
next_verification: Find Indonesian/U.S. meeting notes, Sukarno’s records and the cited media coverage.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green assessed that the Aug. 31 meeting with Sukarno achieved little beyond establishing rapport.
confidence: High that Green made this assessment; not a measure of Sukarno’s private response.
basis_and_limitations: The judgment is one participant’s view.
next_verification: Compare later meeting reports and Indonesian accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On Sept. 10 State suspected a PKI-led campaign and possible central-government collusion or tacit approval behind pressure on U.S. consulates, while acknowledging other motives and possible provincial inability to control extremists.
claim_type: U.S. policy assessment with stated alternatives
confidence: High for U.S. suspicion and caveats; low for coordination absent Indonesian command evidence.
basis_and_limitations: The telegram explicitly says “suspect” and recognizes alternative explanations.
next_verification: Open cited telegrams 598/609 and seek local organizers, police orders and government correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rusk instructed the Embassy to demand a security guarantee and said the United States intended to close Surabaya Consulate without one; he ordered contingency planning to move staff and destroy classified material.
confidence: High for instruction; does not establish closure or destruction occurred.
basis_and_limitations: Distinguish conditional threat and preparation from implementation.
next_verification: Find Embassy response, later orders, property logs and evacuation records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the Sept. 10 meeting record Palar regretted attacks and said Sukarno allowed demonstrations to answer public sentiment but they sometimes got out of hand outside Jakarta.
claim_type: Attributed statement in diplomatic meeting record
confidence: High that the U.S. memo records Palar saying this; explanation itself unverified.
basis_and_limitations: Palar’s account is not direct evidence of Sukarno’s orders or provincial police action.
next_verification: Open the Sept. 17 follow-up and compare Indonesian police/governor records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rusk told Palar that U.S. relations required protection of American personnel and installations and warned Washington would examine Indonesian installations in the United States if U.S. operations became untenable.
confidence: High for warning as recorded; no evidence reciprocal restrictions were applied.
basis_and_limitations: Conditional warning, not implemented closure or retaliatory action.
next_verification: Check subsequent U.S. decisions and Indonesian diplomatic correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On Sept. 14 an NSC staff report said Subandrio had assured Green of U.S. personnel and property safety, while Washington remained skeptical.
confidence: High that Thomson records Green’s report; independent Indonesian confirmation absent.
basis_and_limitations: Not Subandrio’s original written assurance.
next_verification: Obtain Green’s cable, Subandrio record and security measures.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 1 October, Ball asked McNamara to examine evacuation options for U.S. citizens, including ships already in the region and possible British or Australian aircraft at Singapore; McNamara understood the request to concern evacuation while the situation remained unclear.
confidence: High that the officials discussed this contingency; not evidence ships or aircraft were moved or other action undertaken.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d143, paragraphs 1–3. Ball said there were a couple thousand Americans across the islands and did not know whether any further action might follow once events clarified.
next_verification: Read the Oct. 1–4 Ball/Defense contingency calls and compare with CINCPAC movement logs, embassy evacuation orders and allied aircraft records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A later 1 October call recorded Ball asking CIA Director Helms whether the United States could categorically deny CIA operations involvement; Helms said Raborn had authorized a denial and that CIA had nothing to do with events.
confidence: High that the edited FRUS note records Helms’s denial; this is not independent proof of the full scope of CIA activity.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d143 editorial note 2 quotes Ball’s calls with Helms and says one line is not declassified. It records a statement about CIA operations in the Indonesia situation, not a full review of all U.S. contacts or prior policy programs.
next_verification: Seek the original Ball–Helms call memorandum, associated CIA/Director’s files and any separately authorized political-action records; preserve the withheld line as an unresolved gap.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On the afternoon of 1 October, Ball told Fulbright that the apparent coup seemed leftist but that the extent of PKI involvement or foreknowledge remained uncertain; he also described incomplete reports of a counter-move and a possible Army return to the radio station.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. official’s attributed report and assessment
confidence: High for Ball’s recorded assessment; the underlying Indonesian reports and control of units are not independently established by this call.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d144, paragraphs 1–4; the conversation is explicitly marked tentative and says the situation was difficult to know.
next_verification: Compare timestamped RRI transmissions, Indonesian Army and presidential orders, independent press, and other embassies’ same-day cables.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 2 October Ball told Rusk that reports pointed to Suharto’s forces gaining the upper hand and the PKI aligning with the losing side, while Sukarno’s status was still unknown; Rusk speculated that Sukarno might be dead or seriously ill.
confidence: High that the officials exchanged these reports and guesses; not proof of the underlying military alignment or Sukarno’s actual status.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d145, main text and editorial footnote 2. Green’s reported embassy assessment in the footnote also lists several competing explanations for Sukarno’s absence.
next_verification: Compare Sukarno’s diary and radio orders, presidential staff records, army command logs, and Indonesian press for the exact sequence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 4 October Defense Department memorandum reported discovery of the senior officers’ bodies and recorded two incompatible U.S. hypotheses about whether Sukarno had prior knowledge or had been misled; Blouin leaned toward partial foreknowledge but presented this as his assessment.
confidence: High for the memorandum’s competing theories and Blouin’s stated inclination; low for resolving Sukarno’s actual knowledge from this source alone.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d146, paragraphs 1–2 and 4–8. It says some information was conflicting; reports of body condition and the Army’s use of the deaths are mediated through the memo.
next_verification: Compare independent autopsy records, contemporaneous RRI/press, Sukarno’s 1–4 October diary/letters, Air Force and presidential-guard records, and named participants’ testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same 4 October memorandum placed U.S. naval task forces in positions described as possible emergency-evacuation cover and reported TF-76 moving north toward TF-77; it does not describe a combat mission in Indonesia.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. military posture for civilian evacuation contingency
confidence: High that the memorandum reports the positioning and stated contingency; exact track and purpose require operational logs.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d146, evacuation section and editorial note 2, which says Ball, McNamara, McGeorge Bundy, William Bundy and Rusk discussed these forces on Oct. 3–4 for possible emergency evacuation.
next_verification: Obtain CINCPAC/Task Force 76 and 77 deck logs, tasking messages, and the Oct. 3–4 Ball papers; check distance from Indonesian waters.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 6 October State approved the broad guidelines in Green’s 5 October telegram but cautioned against public evidence that the U.S. supported the Army and advised against direct contact with Nasution unless he initiated it, favoring indirect access through senior officers already in contact with the Mission.
claim_type: U.S. diplomatic policy instruction and military liaison channel
confidence: High for the written policy instruction; its receipt and execution in Jakarta need separate records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d148 paragraphs 1, 4–6, read with d147. d148 approves the main lines subject to emphasis and discretion, not every Green proposal as an executed action.
next_verification: Read the full Green telegram, Jakarta follow-up cables, ambassador contact logs and named senior-officer records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State said that the Army did not need U.S. material aid at that point and argued that years of training, civic-action work, MILTAG and repeated assurances to Nasution should already have established that the United States would support Army leaders if they needed help.
claim_type: U.S. official interpretation of prior military ties and reassurance
confidence: High for State’s characterization of its own programs and intended signal; the Army’s independent understanding is not directly documented here.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d148 paragraph 5. This statement concerns the immediate moment and does not establish that material support was never later provided.
next_verification: Compare MAP delivery and training records, MILTAG and DLG communications, Nasution’s papers, Army liaison logs and later aid requests/receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 6 October State reported that a VOA and related information program was already being carried out by citing Indonesian sources and official statements without U.S. editorializing, with similar Indonesia coverage in selected broadcasts outside Indonesia; it planned to reconsider if those source materials dried up.
claim_type: U.S. information-program execution as reported by State
confidence: High that State reported ongoing broadcast activity and its method; actual scripts, transmission reach, audience response and effects are unverified.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d148 paragraph 6. The memo does not include VOA transmission logs or third-country station records. Distinguish this reported activity from Green’s covert Army-contact proposal in d147.
next_verification: Obtain VOA/Federal Broadcast Information Service logs, scripts, distribution schedules, USIA files and partner-station records; compare the cited Indonesian source statements.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 6 October the Department instructed the Embassy to begin moving U.S. families out of Indonesia on international commercial carriers and allowed routine home-leave or medical explanations at the outset to keep the operation unobtrusive.
claim_type: Contemporary evacuation instruction as cited in an official editorial note
confidence: High that FRUS d150 footnote 2 reproduces the instruction’s gist; actual departures and the Embassy’s implementation roster are not shown.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d150 footnote 2 cites Department telegram 401 to Djakarta, October 6, RG 59 POL 23–INDON; original cable not opened independently.
next_verification: Obtain telegram 401 and Embassy departure records, passenger manifests and family notifications.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 7 October Ball told Helms that Green had requested evacuation, commercial carriers were being used as unobtrusively as possible, and the target was for all dependents to depart within three weeks.
confidence: High for Ball’s statement and the intended timeline; it does not establish that all dependents departed or where they went.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d150, 12:05 p.m. telephone memorandum.
next_verification: Check Embassy travel rosters, airline manifests and later completion reports.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 5:30 p.m. call on 7 October Ball and McNamara agreed that the evacuation task force could return slowly to home ports as the situation allowed; the note reports Ball feared civil war within two or three days.
claim_type: Contemporary contingency discussion, reported in an editorial footnote
confidence: High for the call as summarized by FRUS; no ship movement, return route or final order is proved.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d150 footnote 3 cites Johnson Library Ball Papers, telephone conversations on Indonesia.
next_verification: Obtain the original call memorandum, Defense movement orders and CINCPAC/TF76/TF77 logs.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 14 October Colonel Ethel delivered a U.S. oral message about Confrontation to a Nasution aide, who wrote it down and said he would pass it to Nasution; the aide said the reassurance would help the Army feel it was not being pressured from every side. An FRUS footnote cites an October 15 cable reporting that Nasution received the message and was very satisfied, hoping Britain would “lay off.”
claim_type: Reported diplomatic message transmission and recipient reaction
confidence: High that the U.S. record reports message delivery and Nasution’s reported reaction; no Indonesian recipient minute, British response or policy effect is independently checked.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d154 paragraph 1 and footnote 3, which cites Department telegram 2005 to London, October 15; d151/C750 supplies context for the original reassurance.
next_verification: Retrieve telegram 2005, Jakarta 1006, British FO response and any Nasution or Indonesian command record.

atomic_claim_or_observation: An unnamed Nasution aide told Green that the Army was rounding up Chinese businessmen suspected of involvement and trying to determine the Chinese Embassy’s role in the September 30 events; this is a second-hand U.S. report, not proof of the suspects’ conduct or Beijing’s role.
claim_type: Attributed Army contact report concerning Chinese Indonesians and China
confidence: High for what the U.S. cable records; low for the underlying allegation, legal basis, scale or result.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d154 paragraph 2; unnamed aide relayed the statements through Ethel.
next_verification: Check Indonesian arrest and court files, Chinese Embassy records, local Chinese-community testimony and reports from other embassies.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same aide reported that Army units were rounding up Communist cadres but having difficulty locating weapons said to have been distributed; no quantity, recipient list or seizure inventory is provided.
claim_type: Attributed Army liaison report of arrests and weapons search
confidence: High for the cable’s reported statement; actual arrests, weapons locations and operational scope remain unverified.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d154 paragraph 3; unnamed contact.
next_verification: Compare Army and police arrest lists, seizure records, local orders and PKI/paramilitary records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The aide said Antara would be allowed to continue its anti-NEKOLIM line, but at a lower volume; the cable records an interlocutor’s report, not an independently checked press order or newsroom policy.
claim_type: Attributed report about news-agency policy and information control
confidence: High for the reported statement; implementation and editorial changes require Antara records and dated content comparison.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d154 paragraph 4.
next_verification: Compare Antara editions, editor/staff arrests, newsroom instructions and Army press directives.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Nasution aide said he had heard about Green’s approach to Indonesian official Suwito concerning detained missionary Harold Lovestrand and thought the approach could work. The FRUS note says Lovestrand had been held since August 1964, his wife and children were released in March 1965, and he was released on March 23, 1966 after U.S. representations.
claim_type: Personal/diplomatic channel and a detained foreign civilian, as reported by FRUS
confidence: High for the published note’s account; the precise contacts, terms, reason for release and Indonesian file are not shown here.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d154 paragraph 5 and footnote 4; cited Embtel 991 and March 1966 cable are not opened.
next_verification: Find Embassy consular case files, Suwito meeting notes, Indonesian detention register and the release cable; distinguish humanitarian representation from political bargaining.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 17 October Green assessed Sukarno and the Army as two rival but interdependent centers of power, each needing the other while trying to weaken the other; this is an Embassy model of the crisis, not an independently measured balance of authority.
confidence: High for Green’s written assessment; actual command over ministries, provinces and armed units needs Indonesian records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraph 2.A.
next_verification: Compare Presidential, Army, cabinet and regional command orders, appointments and implementation.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green reported that attacks on PKI installations had spread from Jakarta, with central Java under Army control in his account and sustained Communist–non-Communist confrontation in east Java and north Sumatra; he warned of possible escalation but did not provide a local incident list.
claim_type: Contemporary diplomatic reporting and regional risk assessment
confidence: High that Green reported these conditions; low for regional representativeness and attribution without local records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraph 2.C; Embassy analysis refers to observers and unnamed reports.
next_verification: Compare province and district incident chronologies, police logs, press, Army orders and named witness records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green said different versions of the Army’s five demands to Sukarno circulated, with common elements reported as Suharto’s appointment to lead the Army, legal punishment of September 30 participants, reorganization of the Air Force, banning organizations or parties that supported the movement, and replacement of the PKI and Subandrio’s intelligence organization.
claim_type: Contemporary diplomatic report of reported Army demands
confidence: High for the list Green summarized; moderate for whether it was an authoritative Army platform because the cable notes multiple versions.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraph 3.B.
next_verification: Find the original Army memorandum or Nasution/Suharto statement and compare Sukarno’s dated responses.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green reported that by 17 October Sukarno had appointed Suharto to head the Army and agreed to send Air Force chief Omar Dhani abroad, but had not yet named a regular replacement; Green said the Army was proceeding on its own to punish people it considered involved in September 30.
claim_type: Contemporary Embassy report on presidential concessions and Army actions
confidence: High for what the Ambassador reported; appointment/departure dates, legal process and actual punishment require Indonesian decrees and case records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraph 3.C.
next_verification: Check presidential decrees, Air Force personnel orders, court and detention files, and local execution records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green forecast that press and National Front activity would remain contested between Sukarno and Army-aligned forces; he reported the Army remained dissatisfied with Antara and was interrogating and harassing its staff.
claim_type: Contemporary report and forecast about media control
confidence: High for Green’s report and prediction; staff identities, legal basis, article changes and nationwide scope are not established.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraphs 5–6.
next_verification: Examine Antara archives, staff detention records, newsroom directives, newspaper closure orders and National Front minutes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green speculated that Sukarno might seek a “new” or “indigenous” Communist party, while the Army preferred a total PKI ban and might instead press for a single party or National Front with a strong functional-group role; these are projected bargaining positions, not a formed party agreement.
claim_type: Contemporary policy forecast of party-system alternatives
confidence: High that the cable described these possibilities; no outcome should be inferred from this forecast.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraphs 4 and 7.
next_verification: Compare subsequent presidential speeches, Army statements, party bans and National Front reorganization orders.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green’s d156 cable uses explicitly value-laden anti-Communist and religious language when interpreting Nasakom, Muslim political attitudes and relations with China; it is evidence of the Ambassador’s analytical frame, not a representative account of Muslim Indonesians or a neutral description of Nasakom.
confidence: High for the language in the cable; it cannot establish Indonesian religious opinion or the causal effect of the Embassy’s framing.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d156 paragraphs 2.D–E.
next_verification: Compare Indonesian Muslim organizations’ own statements, local publications and dissenting U.S. diplomatic analyses.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On 20 October Green reported that the PKI had suffered major damage to its image, communications and command structure and some organizational damage from arrest, harassment and reported executions; he relayed estimates of roughly one thousand cadres arrested in Jakarta and several hundred executed.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. Embassy report of state repression and estimated casualties
confidence: High that the Embassy reported these estimates; the counts are unverified, one source line is withheld and no names or case register are supplied.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d158 paragraphs 2–4; the cable uses “reportedly” for the arrest/execution counts and describes some evidence as direct but redacted.
next_verification: Obtain underlying Embassy source, Army/police rolls, prison registers, court and death records, and local victim lists.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Green judged that the PKI’s basic organizational potential might recover if the party were again recognized and Army attacks stopped, while arguing that lasting suppression would require an attack on communism as an ideology and associated organizations; he praised the Army’s determination to destroy the PKI.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. ambassadorial estimate and political preference
confidence: High for the stated assessment and preference; it does not measure PKI capacity or establish the consequences of alternative policies.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d158 paragraphs 4–6.
next_verification: Compare PKI membership and regional organization records with subsequent bans, arrests, labour and village-level association restrictions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 22 October memorandum to Johnson, McGeorge Bundy called events a “striking vindication” of U.S. policy since 1963 and the Bunker recommendations, described the Army as courageous and public support as extraordinary, and listed major unknowns including Sukarno’s health and role and Aidit’s whereabouts.
confidence: High for Bundy’s written view; the claim about broad public support was not based on a survey in this memo, and “vindication” is an institutional judgment, not proof of U.S. causal control.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d160, Indonesia section.
next_verification: Compare Johnson/Bundy decision records, earlier policy reviews, Indonesian public opinion evidence and internal dissent.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 29 October tentative analysis, State treated Nasution’s 25 October speech and the public campaign against Subandrio as evidence that Army leaders intended an all-out fight against the PKI despite Sukarno’s opposition.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. policy analysis based on attributed political signals
confidence: High for the Department’s stated assessment; Nasution’s aims and Sukarno’s opposition need the underlying speeches and Indonesian records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraphs 1–2.
next_verification: Read Nasution’s speech, Subandrio campaign materials, Sukarno’s dated response and Army operational orders.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State assessed that Army leaders were trying to separate Sukarno from anti-Army advisers, isolate him and retain the option of using or removing him; this is the Department’s interpretation of Army strategy, not an Army order or proof of an agreed plan.
claim_type: U.S. policy analysis of Army–Presidential power struggle
confidence: High for what the Department wrote; low as independent evidence of the Army’s internal decision-making.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 3.
next_verification: Compare Army leadership meeting records, Sukarno–Nasution communications and later command instructions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State predicted that the Army would increasingly act as Indonesia’s de facto government and might need to form a military or civil–military provisional government because it saw no other organized force able to lead after Nasakom’s collapse; this was a forecast and policy analysis.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. forecast of succession and government formation
confidence: High for the forecast’s text; it does not establish that the Army had already decided to seize formal governing power.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraphs 4–5.
next_verification: Compare October–December presidential, cabinet, Army and KOTI orders and provincial responses.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State described the PKI as retreating amid “mass attacks encouraged by the Army” and forecast possible strikes, sabotage or guerrilla action; the Department’s expectation does not establish that PKI leadership had ordered such a response or that the attacks were centrally directed.
claim_type: Contemporary intelligence/policy scenario and attributed description
confidence: High for the wording and scenario in the Department paper; operational attribution and local events remain unverified.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 4.
next_verification: Check Embassy situation reports, PKI orders, regional security files and local incident records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State advised that if Army leaders sought U.S. views, Washington should encourage a civil–military coalition rather than a military junta or purely civilian government; it saw long-standing U.S.–Indonesian Army service ties as an influence channel.
claim_type: U.S. political strategy recommendation and influence channel
confidence: High for the proposed guidance; no evidence in this document that the Army asked for, received or followed the advice.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraphs 7–8.
next_verification: Find follow-up instructions, Army Attaché contacts, message receipts and Indonesian government negotiations.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State proposed that food could be supplied through the International Red Cross if direct U.S. or other outside help embarrassed Army leaders; it listed Japan, Brazil, Malaysia, Thailand, Taiwan and South Korea as possible rice suppliers.
confidence: High for the proposed channel and listed countries; no shipment, funding or Indonesian receipt is shown.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 8.d.
next_verification: Trace Red Cross discussions, donor-country decisions, rice purchase and shipping documents, and Indonesian receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State proposed expert advice and possible IMF/partner assistance for Indonesia’s currency and credit crisis, while linking this option to a change in Indonesia’s recent attitude toward the IMF and other potential partners.
claim_type: Contingent international financial and policy channel
confidence: High for the Department’s proposal and conditional framing; no IMF agreement or disbursement is established.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 8.e.
next_verification: Compare IMF Board records, Indonesian Finance Ministry requests, donor meeting notes and subsequent credit transfers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State said small arms and equipment might be needed if Army operations against the PKI expanded and proposed preparing for that contingency; this was not an arms authorization, purchase or delivery.
confidence: High for the proposal; no specific model, quantity, recipient, funding or approved logistics route is given.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 8.f; later planning is separately documented in d164/C1232.
next_verification: Trace d164 onward, arms stock checks, third-country procurement, shipping, recipient lists and serial-number records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State considered using petroleum requirements to propose a de facto pause in nationalization of U.S. oil interests, so oil companies could provide full support to the Army and Indonesian economy; the document records an idea, not an agreed moratorium or company action.
claim_type: Economic leverage and private-company support proposal
confidence: High for the proposal; no corporate decision, oil supply contract or policy adoption is shown.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraph 8.h.
next_verification: Compare State/Commerce oil policy, Caltex and Stanvac files, Indonesian nationalization instruments and company supply records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: State expected the Army might first seek Japanese support and recommended quiet U.S.–Japanese consultations, with later consultation with Britain, Australia and others; Japanese aid, coordination and influence were still proposals.
claim_type: Third-country diplomatic coordination and aid-channel proposal
confidence: High for the Department’s stated expectation and recommendation; no agreement or completed aid program is established by d163.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 paragraphs 9–10; d164/C1232 records a subsequent interagency discussion, not an executed transfer.
next_verification: Obtain Japanese MOFA/Prime Minister records, London/Canberra responses, donor instruments and shipment/receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The FRUS editorial note to d163 says the Jakarta Embassy on 2 November agreed with the broad analysis but emphasized that the Sukarno–Army contest remained unsettled, the Army still needed Sukarno and some leaders revered him, and the Embassy expected a long political struggle.
claim_type: Later Embassy reaction reported by an official editorial note
confidence: High for what the FRUS editor reports; the cited November 2 telegram 1304 is not reproduced or independently opened.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d163 editorial note 2, citing telegram 1304 from Djakarta.
next_verification: Open telegram 1304 and compare with subsequent presidential and Army decisions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Airgram A-398 separates two enclosures: an unclassified list of PKI leadership bodies as they stood after the May 1965 plenary, and a Secret, fragmentary report on leaders’ whereabouts explicitly based on limited information.
claim_type: Contemporary source scope, classification and information-quality statement
confidence: High for the wording and markings on the scanned original; the document does not establish that the status enclosure was complete.
basis_and_limitations: A-398 original scan, cover and digital pp.1–6; enclosure 1 on pp.2–4 is marked unclassified; enclosure 2 on pp.5–6 is marked Secret. FRUS d185 summarizes its limited-information caveat.
next_verification: Compare the enclosure copies sent to State/other posts with any sanitized Indonesian copy; request original A-74 and attachments.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A-398 warned that Embassy reports of prominent PKI leaders’ arrests often rested on suspect evidence and that alleged confessions were widely falsified; it cited an alleged Njono confession that seemed unaware of changes to the Politburo made at the May 1965 plenary.
claim_type: Contemporary Embassy assessment of evidence quality
confidence: High that the Embassy made this assessment; whether each particular confession was fabricated is not independently resolved by A-398.
basis_and_limitations: A-398 original scan, digital p.1, paragraph 1; FRUS d185 editorial note, paragraph 2. This is a warning about the evidence available to the Embassy, not independent proof about Njono’s interrogation or the authenticity of every confession.
next_verification: Find the alleged Njono confession and compare its text with the May 1965 Politburo roster, interrogation records and independent custody evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a June 1990 letter, Robert J. Martens acknowledged passing names of PKI leaders and senior cadres to non-Communist forces; he said the material came entirely from Indonesian Communist publications, covered at most a few thousand senior officials rather than rank and file, and that he acted without seeking or receiving Embassy permission.
claim_type: Retrospective first-person account of information source, transfer and authorization
confidence: High that Martens publicly made this account; its accuracy about the full list, total number, authorization chain and recipients is not independently established by the letter.
basis_and_limitations: Martens, Washington Post letter to the editor, archived June 1/2, 1990; FRUS d185 reproduces the letter. Distinguish Martens’s account from Green’s 1966 A-74 report of a sanitized A-398 version made available to the Indonesian Government.
next_verification: Compare with the complete interview transcripts/tapes, list copies, contemporaneous Embassy clearance records and recipient registers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 1991 oral-history interview, Martens recalled that a chief aide to Adam Malik visited his house a few weeks after September 30 and asked for help; Martens says he passed basic material assembled from the Communist press to the aide, who took it to Malik, who “apparently” gave it to the Army, while Martens said he did not know what effect it had.
claim_type: Retrospective oral testimony about a possible interpersonal information-transfer route
confidence: High for the content of Martens’s published recollection; low for exact timing, identity/receipt at each later link, whether this was the same sanitized A-398 copy, and any operational effect.
basis_and_limitations: ADST excerpt from Martens oral history, paragraphs shown under “I had assembled all this unclassified data” (2016 web edition); the interview itself uses approximate language and the full tape/transcript was not compared.
next_verification: Read the complete ADST transcript and Kadane’s deposited recordings/transcripts; identify the aide from independent Indonesian sources and locate Malik/Army receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A July 1990 New York Times report said interviewees did not dispute that names were passed to Indonesians, but found disagreement over whether Martens acted alone or senior Embassy/CIA officials coordinated the transfer and over the list’s importance; excerpts of Kadane’s recorded interviews appeared ambiguous on some officials’ advance knowledge or approval.
claim_type: Contemporary journalistic account of a disputed retrospective investigation
confidence: High for what the published article reported; the article is not a substitute for the underlying tapes, transcripts, transfer records or Indonesian files and does not settle the dispute.
basis_and_limitations: Michael Wines, “C.I.A. Tie Asserted in Indonesia Purge,” New York Times, 12 July 1990, full text through an Asia-Pacific Solidarity Network reprint, lines 17–50; compare Kadane’s May 21 report and Martens’s June letter.
next_verification: Retrieve the reporter’s full source transcripts, Kadane’s original recordings and complete Green/Lydman/Masters interviews; compare each exact question and response.

atomic_claim_or_observation: GerakIngatan catalogs a 1978 Komitee Indonesië congress titled Het Andere Indonesia about development aid and the perspective of ordinary Indonesians; the catalog cites IISH solidarity-movement collection COLL00284.

next_verification: Retrieve permitted scan/proceedings; identify date, venue, participants, IGGI-related proposals and independently check implementation.
