atomic_claim_or_observation: In an April 10, 1997 letter, reporter Kathy Kadane said she had transferred her taped interviews, notes and a small group of documents, including some declassified cables, to the National Security Archive at George Washington University.
claim_type: Reporter’s statement about research records and archival provenance
confidence: High that Kadane publicly made this statement; the deposit inventory and current physical or access status of each item are not independently verified.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB publisher-hosted exchange, Kadane letter, paragraph 2 (1997). This confirms a published statement, not that a particular tape or full transcript can now be located or accessed.
next_verification: Locate the National Security Archive accession, box/folder inventory, and access rules; identify recordings, notes, exhibits and any restrictions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the 1997 NYRB letter, Kadane reported that the Pentagon supplied jeeps and that U.S. officials supplied “dozens” of field radios to Indonesian Army forces during the post-September 30 crisis; she separately attributed the Collins KWM-2 procurement to CIA in the next part of her account.
claim_type: Retrospective journalist-reported allegation of logistical supply
confidence: High for what Kadane reported; low/unverified for the number, timing, recipient units, shipment and use because no itemized delivery record is attached or located.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Kadane letter, paragraphs 4–5. The article distinguishes Pentagon jeeps, general U.S. radios, and an unnamed former Embassy official’s more specific CIA/Collins-radio account; it does not append a shipment manifest, receipt or operational log.
next_verification: Seek Pentagon/CIA procurement and surplus records, Clark Field inventory and flight logs, serial numbers, Kostrad and recipient-unit inventories, and Indonesian-side receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Kadane reported that an unnamed former Embassy official described CIA-provided Collins KWM-2 high-frequency radios held at Clark Field in the Philippines, secretly flown to Indonesia by the U.S. Air Force and delivered to Suharto’s Kostrad headquarters by Pentagon representatives.
confidence: High that Kadane published this attributed account; low/unverified for model, number, staging location, flight, recipient and date because the source’s identity and supporting records are unavailable here.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Kadane letter, paragraphs 5–6; source is an unnamed former official as presented in Kadane’s article. Do not merge with the distinct three Motorola P-31 radios in FRUS d155 or the later HF communications program in d175/d211.
next_verification: Find CIA logistics files, USAF C-130/Clark Field movement records, radio serial/inventory records, Kostrad receipts and the full interview and notes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Kadane said a former U.S. official described the CIA providing Indonesian Army radio frequencies to the National Security Agency in advance, an NSA site in Southeast Asia intercepting and translating the traffic, and resulting reporting being sent to Washington alongside Embassy reporting.
confidence: High for the published allegation; low/unverified for the actual intercepts, location, tasking, translations, reporting chain and use because no NSA/CIA collection records or interview tape were examined.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Kadane letter, paragraphs 6–7. FRUS d175 documents a proposed covert communications system and U.S. links but does not by itself prove NSA monitoring of that system.
next_verification: Search NSA/CIA declassified SIGINT and liaison files, frequency-allocation records, site logs, translation reports and the Kadane interview tape/transcript.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Kadane reported that an unnamed former U.S. official said NSA intercepts included orders from Suharto’s intelligence unit to kill specific persons at specified locations.
claim_type: Retrospective journalist-reported allegation about target-specific lethal orders
confidence: High that Kadane published this allegation; unverified as an actual intercept or order, with no Indonesian command record, victim identification, signal transcript or independent source located.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Kadane letter, paragraph 7. Keep the alleged order, whether transmitted, whether received, whether acted upon and any resulting death as separate questions.
next_verification: Obtain the alleged intercept transcript and underlying NSA report; identify the unit/person/location only from original records; compare against Indonesian orders and independent victim/custody records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the 1997 NYRB exchange, Robert L. Barry rejected the theory that Suharto and possibly the CIA conspired in the 1965 coup and aftermath, and argued that the ensuing violence was more readily explained as a spontaneous release of pent-up social tensions.
confidence: High that Barry published this interpretation; it is not contemporaneous evidence of 1965 operations or a substitute for archival corroboration.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Barry letter, paragraphs 7–9. Barry identifies himself there as U.S. Ambassador to Indonesia in 1992–1995, not as a 1965 witness.
next_verification: Assess the 1965 causal question from contemporary Indonesian, U.S., British, Australian, Dutch and other records, plus independent local histories; do not treat this letter as direct evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In her reply to Barry in the same 1997 exchange, Jeri Laber disputed his “spontaneous explosion” explanation, citing scholarly agreement about Army arming and inciting local attacks and asserting evidence of U.S. moral and financial support; she called for release of Indonesian and U.S. records.
claim_type: Later editor’s published interpretation and evidence claim
confidence: High that Laber published this response; the scholarly sources and underlying financial records must be checked independently and are not established by the letter alone.
basis_and_limitations: NYRB exchange, Laber reply, paragraphs 10–13. Her statement records an interpretation and a pointer to other evidence, not a substitute for those sources.
next_verification: Trace her cited article and the primary evidence it references; compare with Indonesian Army orders, local organizational records, and independently documented U.S. finance.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Bunnell states that his 1990 reconstruction relied primarily on U.S. government documents and interviews with more than 75 former American officials; he describes Jakarta dissertation research in 1963–65 and says his 1981–82 Indonesian-source work had very limited success.
confidence: High that the article describes its method this way; the underlying interview set and notes are not available in this record.
basis_and_limitations: Bunnell, pp. 29 and note 5; full Cornell-hosted article sections read.
next_verification: Locate Bunnell’s interview notes and any deposited papers; identify which claims rely on Sukendro or the same former officials.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Bunnell reports that General Sukendro confirmed in interviews in 1981–82 that the U.S. had secretly supplied medicines, radios and small arms through the CIA station in Bangkok.
claim_type: Retrospective recipient account reported by a historian
confidence: High that Bunnell published this statement; medium for the reported interview content; actual delivery timing, quantities, radio types, recipients and weapon use remain unverified because the interview record is not open here.
basis_and_limitations: Bunnell, p. 60 and note 152; compare FRUS d171 (Nov. 5: no discussion of providing weapons or radios beyond approved medicine), d173 (Nov. 10 request), d175/d211 (distinct communications proposal and later stages). Do not treat other authors repeating Bunnell as independent confirmation.
next_verification: Find Bunnell’s Sukendro interview recording, notes or deposited papers; locate Bangkok station procurement, shipment and Army receipt/issue records, especially small-arms serials and recipient units.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Bunnell concludes that the United States was not a prime instigator of the failed September 30 Movement or the massacres, but was an important and knowing accomplice to the Army-led campaign; he also cautions that the extent of CIA activity could not be finally judged without withheld records.
claim_type: Retrospective historian’s causal and political interpretation
confidence: High that Bunnell states this conclusion; the causal interpretation remains the author’s analysis and must not be substituted for the user’s political judgment.
basis_and_limitations: Bunnell, pp. 30 and 60; he explicitly discusses incomplete/declassified records and uncertainty about the CIA station.
next_verification: Compare with later archival releases and differently argued scholarship; keep the full causal chain and the user’s judgment separate.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 1987 interview Green said he personally ordered all fourteen emergency walkie-talkies held by the U.S. Embassy transferred to Suharto, without a request, to provide internal security and signal U.S. concern; in the preceding account he says his first private meeting with Suharto was May 29, 1966, but gives no exact handover date.
period: Following the interview’s May 29, 1966 context; recalled 1987
claim_type: Retrospective first-person testimony about a separate Embassy equipment transfer
confidence: High for what Green said; medium for the transfer as a firsthand but 21-year-later account; low for exact date/model/serial, signed receipt and effect. Do not merge with three P-31 sets discussed in the October 1965 telegram.
basis_and_limitations: ADST oral history, interviewer Robert J. Martens, transcript around pp. 25–27; compare FRUS d155, which records a separate three-set P-31 offer and planned Oct. 14 turnover.
next_verification: Find Green’s report and Bundy response cable, Embassy emergency radio inventory, issue/receipt records and Suharto security-office inventory.

atomic_claim_or_observation: On Nov. 4, State authorized processing Sukendro’s medical-supply request but said it was handling a separately mentioned communications-equipment matter in the Jakarta–Washington channel and did not want it discussed with Sukendro; it also said not to pursue arms with him at that point. The wording about equipment “passed from Djakarta” is partly redacted.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. policy instruction with redacted operational reference
confidence: High for the unredacted instruction; low/unresolved for what equipment moved, sender/recipient, date and route because the phrase is redacted.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d170, paragraphs 1–5; State says it is “looking separately” at the communications issue and limits contact with Sukendro.
next_verification: Request the full RG 59 telegram and referenced Jakarta 1333/State 749 cables; compare Embassy equipment logs and Army receipt records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Nov. 5 Bangkok cable records that Sukendro designated an Army colonel to discuss small-arms needs and a police colonel to bring a communications-equipment list, but explicitly says there was no discussion of U.S. provision of weapons or communications gear beyond the medical aid already approved.
claim_type: Contemporary covert-liaison record and aid-stage distinction
confidence: High for the cable’s wording and recorded meeting; it does not show whether requests were later approved or delivered.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d171 paragraphs 1–5 and footnote 6; distinguish the forthcoming lists from an agreement to supply.
next_verification: Read the referenced missing cables and Nov. 6 guidance; find later decisions, Bangkok station procurement and Army acknowledgements.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a Nov. 10 Bangkok meeting report, Sukendro said senior Army leaders in Jakarta lacked portable voice radios and requested about a dozen sets for Nasution, Suharto, Umar, Sukendro and other senior officers, plus the Paracommandos and possibly a guard battalion.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. cable reporting an Army communications request
confidence: High that the U.S. cable records these named proposed users; the Army’s actual inventory and need are not independently verified by this report.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d173 paragraphs 3–4. This is a requested system, distinct from d155 P-31 offer and the later 303 proposal.
next_verification: Find the original Sukendro request/list, Army communications inventory and any purchase or serial/receipt log.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same Nov. 11 cable records a separate request for a Jakarta-based voice circuit connecting Medan, Palembang, Bandung, Semarang, Surabaya, Makassar and Banjarmasin, possibly Yogyakarta, plus a Central Java tactical communications study; Sukendro described these as Army requirements and said the existing long-range voice net was lacking.
confidence: High for the reported list and attributed assessment; actual network coverage, equipment loss and operational consequences require local records.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d173 paragraphs 5–7; this was a second network concept separate from portable sets.
next_verification: Find Army signal corps plans, city-level radio inventories, frequencies, local command logs and Indonesian procurement/installation records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Nov. 11 Embassy proposal said the Army lacked funds and, if Washington acceded, commercially available radios could be covertly procured and delivered through a transfer point whose text is redacted; Sukendro said the Army could receive and forward them. The Embassy estimated about $40,000 for a stock configuration with voice and CW capability.
claim_type: Contemporary covert procurement and logistics proposal
confidence: High for the proposal and redacted route reference; it is conditional and does not establish approval, payment, shipment, receipt or operation.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d173 paragraphs 8–9 and footnotes 6–7; the estimate is not a realized invoice.
next_verification: Obtain the missing follow-on telegram 952, the NARA RG 59 file, 303 minutes, purchase/freight documents, transfer-point records and recipient receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A FRUS editorial note to d173 reports that on Nov. 12 the Department told Australian, New Zealand and British Embassy officials that the U.S. had agreed to send $100,000 in medicines and was seriously considering $50,000 in commercial communications equipment; the cited underlying Telegram 373 was not reproduced in this source.
claim_type: Official editorial report of allied diplomatic notification
confidence: High for what the published FRUS note reports; the original cable, allied reactions and actual medical/radio delivery remain unverified.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d173 footnote 7; compare its $50,000 consideration with the Bangkok Embassy’s separate $40,000 stock-item estimate in paragraph 9.
next_verification: Retrieve Telegram 373 and U.S./Australian/New Zealand/British diplomatic files; trace the medical shipment and any communications contracts or dispatches.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Brad Simpson’s 2010 essay states that covert U.S. assistance apparently included small arms delivered to the Indonesian Army through the CIA station in Bangkok; the publisher-hosted version read here supplies no inline note for that sentence.
confidence: High that Simpson published the assertion; low as independent confirmation of delivery because the article’s local source trail is not shown and it may rely on the Bunnell/Sukendro interview or the same U.S. records.
basis_and_limitations: Inside Indonesia 99, paragraphs 27–36; compare Bunnell p. 60/note 152 and the explicit initial holds in d170/d171. Treat as historiography, not receipt evidence.
next_verification: Trace Simpson’s cited chapter/archive notes in Economists with Guns; seek declassified CIA station records and Indonesian Army weapons issue/receipt lists.

atomic_claim_or_observation: FRUS d177 reports, through its note citing the Nov. 16 Embassy Airgram 331, that Sukarno told the Cabinet on Nov. 6 that former Ambassador Howard Jones had given an unnamed Indonesian Rp150 million to spread “Free World” ideology. This establishes that Green’s cable recorded the allegation, not that Jones made a payment.
claim_type: Contemporary U.S. record of a reported Indonesian presidential accusation
confidence: High that the U.S. cable reports the accusation; unverified whether any payment occurred, who the unnamed recipient was, or what the funds were for.
basis_and_limitations: FRUS d177 footnote 3 points to Embassy Airgram 331, Nov. 16, POL 2-1 INDON; neither the speech transcript nor underlying airgram was opened. The footnote is not an accounting record.
next_verification: Retrieve Airgram 331 and the Nov. 6 Cabinet speech/Indonesian press reports; identify the named recipient only from primary evidence; trace any U.S. appropriations, disbursement or covert-action accounts and compare competing U.S./Indonesian accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a printed excerpt of Kathy Kadane’s December 1989 interview with Edward Masters, Masters assents to the account that Martens and others compiled PKI biographical index cards in an interagency team in the Embassy political section, that CIA material was cross-indexed with other information, and that PKI names were circulated among Embassy officials for their own additions.
claim_type: Selected retrospective oral-history testimony about data collection and interagency handling
confidence: High that the published excerpt prints Masters’s assent; medium that it captures the full interview context or complete process, because the audio and unabridged transcript were not heard/read.
basis_and_limitations: CovertAction Information Bulletin no. 35, p. 59, section “The Indonesia Transcripts”; the interview is attributed to Dec. 1989. Kadane’s prompts supply some of the description; Masters’s replies are brief. The excerpt gives no index-card files, names, handling logs, dates, scope of CIA inputs or use by Indonesian recipients.
next_verification: Locate the original Kadane audio/transcript and notes at the National Security Archive; seek Martens’s card files, Embassy circulation records, CIA cross-index entries and transfer/receipt documentation; compare against FRUS d185/A-74 and Indonesian list copies.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a May 14, 1990 interview excerpt, Jack Lydman agreed that senior Embassy officials cooperated in supervising/checking names, acknowledged that names of arrested or killed people were reported back from Suharto’s headquarters, but said he did not remember the exact sequence and could not identify the principal U.S. contact with Ali Murtopo.
claim_type: Selected retrospective testimony on Embassy oversight and feedback reporting
confidence: High that the printed excerpt contains these statements; medium for the underlying chain and its completeness, given the selected excerpt and lack of audio.
basis_and_limitations: CovertAction Information Bulletin no. 35, pp. 58–59. The excerpt simultaneously supports senior-level cooperation and records Lydman’s uncertainty about the precise return chain/contact; neither should be dropped when summarizing it.
next_verification: Obtain full audio/transcript and Kadane’s notes; compare Green, Masters, Tovar, Ethel and Martens accounts with Embassy reporting, Martens list files, Ali Murtopo/Suharto headquarters records and any returned-name logs.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a Dec. 20, 1989 excerpt, Kadane told Marshall Green that Masters had identified a group decision for Martens to disseminate names to an Army emissary, listing Green, CIA station chief Hugh Tovar, Masters, Defense Attaché Willis Ethel and Lydman; Green’s printed response is “Yeah.”
claim_type: Selected retrospective testimony attributed to the Ambassador about authorization
confidence: High that the excerpt prints this question, list and response; medium for its precise meaning because the interviewer supplies the group description and the full question/answer context is unavailable.
basis_and_limitations: CovertAction Information Bulletin no. 35, p. 59. The brief affirmation does not establish the date, exact material, number of names, recipient identity, written authorization, intended use, subsequent transfer or effect.
next_verification: Hear the complete Dec. 20 Green recording and read Kadane’s transcript/notes; locate Embassy/303/State approval or distribution records, Martens list copies, and Army intermediary receipts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a Dec. 18, 1989 excerpt, Green said he did not know whether U.S. officials furnished information in the breakup of the PKI and suggested asking Martens; in the same excerpt he said the United States had more information than Indonesians and thought it might have been superior.
claim_type: Selected retrospective testimony showing uncertainty and an attributed intelligence assessment
confidence: High that the printed excerpt contains Green’s statements; the asserted comparative quality of U.S. and Indonesian information is Green’s impression, not an independently measured comparison.
basis_and_limitations: CovertAction Information Bulletin no. 35, p. 59. The full recording, exact question context, relevant U.S. files and Indonesian intelligence holdings were not reviewed.
next_verification: Obtain the full Green interview and compare it with Martens’s files, CIA/Embassy holdings and surviving Indonesian Army/G-2 material.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Cornell University’s finding aid for George McTurnan Kahin’s papers lists Box 81 Folder 7 as “Kadane interviews” (1995), Box 95 Folder 40 as “Kadane. Embassy list: 1965 articles” (1990), and nearby 1965 coup files; the folder contents were not examined.
confidence: High that the indexed finding aid lists these box/folder titles; no claim about the contents, provenance or presence of the NSA tapes is established.
basis_and_limitations: Cornell RMC legacy guide, collection 14-27-3146. The legacy URL currently redirects from the full guide; the indexed record was reviewed. Catalog titles alone do not show that folders contain recordings or particular documents.
next_verification: Contact Cornell RMC for folder descriptions/access and inspect Box 81 Folder 7 and Box 95 Folders 39–40; compare any material with Kadane’s separately reported National Security Archive deposit.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 2011 transcript that cites Revolusi Belum Selesai I, p. 82, presents Sukarno’s Nov. 6, 1965 Cabinet speech as saying he had evidence that America, through Ambassador Howard Jones, gave Rp150 million to an unnamed person; the excerpt says a handover/receipt document and sworn statement identified the intended purpose as promoting “Free World ideology.” Sukarno also remarked that Jones had been personally good to him. This is the content attributed to the speech, not proof of the payment or receipt.
period: 1965-11-06; transcribed in a 2003 collection and 2011 blog
claim_type: Retrospective printed-transcription report of a presidential allegation
confidence: High that the 2011 page prints this wording and cites the collection/page; medium-low that the transcription is exact because the book and original speech record were not directly inspected. No underlying payment/receipt established.
basis_and_limitations: The blog page gives a speech title/date/page and prints a short excerpt; the ITB catalog confirms the 2003 collection exists. FRUS d177 independently reports the allegation’s gist from an Embassy Airgram but does not reproduce the alleged receipt.
next_verification: Inspect the 2003 collection pp.82–83; locate the Nov. 6 Cabinet stenogram/audio/minutes and identify the “handover/receipt” document; search NARA RG 59 Airgram 331 and Jones/Embassy funds, covert-action disbursement, liaison and recipient records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 2011 transcript citing Revolusi Belum Selesai I, p. 302, presents Sukarno’s Dec. 18, 1965 appeal to HMI in Bogor as saying he had reports from the East Java governor, the East Java military commander and his own information of killings of Pemuda Rakyat/PKI members and sympathizers in East and Central Java, and of threats against people who cared for or buried bodies; he urged Indonesians not to split the nation. This records Sukarno’s reported awareness and public appeal as transcribed, not independent proof of each local incident or number.
period: 1965-12-18; transcribed in a 2003 collection and 2011 blog
claim_type: Retrospective printed-transcription report of contemporaneous speech and attributed incoming reports
confidence: High that the blog page prints the excerpt and cites the collection/page; medium-low for exact transcription pending direct collation. Low as independent corroboration of specific deaths because underlying reports/cases are not reproduced.
basis_and_limitations: The text directly attributes the information to named offices and Sukarno’s own information but gives no dates, locations, names, orders or supporting documents. The speech collection itself and contemporaneous governor/military reports were not opened.
next_verification: Inspect volume I p.302 and adjacent pages; search the East Java governor’s office, Kodam/Brawijaya and Kabinet Dwikora reporting for the cited reports; compare local victim, burial, police, hospital, religious and family records in East and Central Java.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Najjarine and Cottle report that a 1945 Cabinet memorandum assigned the political-warfare/propaganda function of short-wave broadcasting to the Department of External Affairs; the cited original memorandum has not been read here.
claim_type: Later scholarly report of a government policy record
confidence: Moderate for the underlying arrangement; high that the article cites it
basis_and_limitations: S814 pp.50–51 and notes 10, 13–14 cite NAA A4940/1 C1344. The original record is registered as the uninspected lead S815.
next_verification: Retrieve and read the Cabinet memorandum; confirm the division between political policy, administration and broadcaster editorial authority.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Najjarine and Cottle report that Cabinet approved a Radio Australia booster-station proposal in 1963 and authorized additional funds; this policy approval does not establish completion, expenditure, transmission range or audience effect.
claim_type: Later scholarly report of Cabinet submission and decision
confidence: Moderate for the underlying Cabinet action until the cited submission and minute are read
basis_and_limitations: S814 p.50–51 and notes 16–17 cite NAA A4940/1 C1344. The submission and minute are registered as uninspected leads S816–S817.
next_verification: Inspect the submission, decision, final expenditure, construction and engineering records; establish coverage and Indonesian audience reach.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 2003 study reports that Richard Woolcott’s 12 October 1965 guidance for Radio Australia favored news selection that would not help the PKI and would highlight reports discrediting it and associating it with the 30 September Movement.
claim_type: Later scholarly reconstruction citing a contemporaneous Australian memorandum
confidence: Moderate for the reported memo contents; no direct proof here of actual script changes or broadcasts
basis_and_limitations: S814 pp.52–53, note 60 cites NAA A1838/280, 3034/2/1/8 Part 2; that memo is an uninspected lead S818.
next_verification: Read the Woolcott memorandum, underlying drafts, ABC/DEA editing correspondence, broadcast scripts, transmission logs and audience/reception records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Two scholarly accounts report that Shann’s 5 November 1965 Cablegram 1340 conveyed an Indonesian Army information officer’s preferences for Radio Australia: do not portray the Army as acting alone, mention Muslim and Christian youth groups, and avoid describing the Army as Western or right-wing; the cited cable has not been directly read and its archival locators differ.
claim_type: Layered diplomatic report as reproduced in later scholarship
confidence: Moderate for the reported cable content; low for actual broadcast adoption or effect
basis_and_limitations: S814 pp.53–54, note 34; S050 pp.166–167, note 83. The cable is registered as uninspected lead S819. The articles cite three possible NAA locations; they may be copies or citation discrepancies.
next_verification: Retrieve A1838/280 file Part 1, A1838/273 Radio Australia file Part 3, and A6364/JA1965/10; compare the records and then inspect scripts and broadcast logs.

atomic_claim_or_observation: David Easter reports that at a 2–3 November 1965 Bangkok meeting Sukendro asked Malaysian official Ghazali Shafie that Radio Malaysia avoid giving the Army excessive credit or criticizing Sukarno and instead emphasize alleged PKI atrocities and the party’s role in the coup; the meeting record is not directly read here.
claim_type: Later scholarly report of a British diplomatic meeting record
confidence: Moderate for the meeting content as reported; low for what Radio Malaysia actually broadcast
basis_and_limitations: S046 pp.60–61 and note 70 cite TNA FO 371/181457. The contemporaneous record is registered as uninspected lead S820.
next_verification: Obtain the record of meeting dated 10 November 1965, compare with Malaysian diplomatic/Radio Malaysia files, scripts, logs and Indonesian reception.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Easter reports that Sukendro also sought Malaysian help for a political campaign against Foreign Minister Subandrio and offered background material; this remains a secondary report of the same uninspected meeting record.
claim_type: Later scholarly report of a British diplomatic meeting record
confidence: Moderate that the article reports this request; low for delivery, use or political effect
basis_and_limitations: S046 pp.60–61 and note 70 cite TNA FO 371/181457. The record is registered as uninspected lead S820.
next_verification: Inspect the original meeting record, Ghazali’s forwarded report, Malaysian authorization, any distributed Subandrio dossier, and contemporaneous Indonesian responses.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Easter reports that on 5 November 1965 an Indonesian military contact cautioned U.S. officials against broadcasts that could imply U.S. approval of Army actions; the cited telegram is not directly read here.
claim_type: Later scholarly report of a U.S. Embassy telegram
confidence: Moderate for the report’s existence and topic; low for the exact contact, wording, and implementation until the telegram is read
